title: introduce rag embedded debug probes and telemetry quickstart
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a new RAG quickstart that demonstrates embedding lightweight debug probes and telemetry hooks for local development and production observability. Recommended for teams instrumenting RAG workflows for latency, cache hits, and tool-calling traces.
body: Summary: This PR adds a new quickstart that shows developers how to wire embedded debug probes into a small Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) agent. The quickstart covers local developer ergonomics (live probes, toggles), structured telemetry events (span names, severity levels), and an optional lightweight relay for shipping telemetry to hosted observability backends. Motivation: Teams building RAG agents often struggle to get actionable signals from fast-moving tool-calling paths and KV cache interactions. This quickstart provides an opinionated, minimal instrumented example that is easy to drop into existing RAG microservices and runs with the Redwood SDKs. It is intentionally small (single-node dev mode) and focuses on observability primitives rather than a full production collector. What changed (high level commits): 1) feat: add quickstart skeleton and README with setup and walkthrough (initial commit) 2) feat: embed debug-probe helpers in example agent (probe lifecycle, sampling toggle) 3) feat: add telemetry relayer example (file sink + optional HTTP forwarder) 4) docs: add architecture diagram and troubleshooting tips 5) tests: add smoke test for probe lifecycle and CI integration Notes on design: - Embedded probes are designed for low overhead: sampling rate defaults to 0.05 and can be bumped via environment variable for local debugging. - Probes emit structured JSON lines with fields: timestamp, probe_id, probe_type, duration_ms, tags, trace_id, span_id. - The optional relayer demonstrates how to convert probe lines to OTLP/Jaeger/Redwood Console events; it is intentionally separate from the agent to keep quickstart minimal. Files changed (high level): - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/README.md (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/example-agent/main.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/example-agent/probes.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/relayer/README.md (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/relayer/relayer.py (new) - quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes/test/test_probes.py (new) - docs/images/rag-probes-arch.svg (new) Short commit summaries: - a1f3c2e feat: quickstart scaffold and README with runbook - b7d9a11 feat: probes helper and context manager + sampling - c4e5f82 feat: relayer example and OTLP mapping - d91a7b0 test: add probe lifecycle smoke test and CI job CI/Checks: - GitHub Actions: python-unit-tests (pass) - Lint: ruff/black (pass) - Docs build: mkdocs (pass, warnings fixed in final commit) - Quickstart smoke matrix: local run & patch tests (pass) Testing performed: - Local end-to-end: executed the example agent in dev mode, toggled sampling to 1.0, verified probe lines written to file sink, and verified relayer converts to OTLP JSON envelope. - Unit: test_probes covers probe lifecycle, start/stop semantics, and sampling edge cases. - Manual: ran the quickstart against a small local vector store (sqlite) and validated cache-hit probe emission for prefix-cached responses. Review conversation (high level): - Riley Park: Requested clearer guidance for production vs dev usage and asked to lower default sampling in README. Response: lowered default sampling to 0.05 and added a prominent WARNING block in README. - Sofia Martinez: Asked for a one-click dev run command and CI smoke test. Response: added a github workflow quickstart-smoke that runs the example agent for 10s and asserts probes appear. - Liam O'Connor: Minor feedback on naming (probe -> debug_probe) and suggested tracing span_id presence; both addressed. Migration/rollout notes: - This is a docs/quickstart-only change; no runtime library changes. Safe to merge with docs cadence. - If teams adopt relayer in production, recommend routing to a buffered collector and enforcing backpressure; added a short paragraph to README. How to run locally (excerpt): - git checkout feature/rag-embedded-probes-qs - cd quickstarts/rag-embedded-probes - python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate - pip install -r example-agent/requirements.txt - env REDWOOD_PROBE_SAMPLING=1.0 python example-agent/main.py - tail -f /tmp/rag-probes.log to watch probe lines Observability guidance included: - Probe taxonomy and suggested naming conventions (e.g., probe_type:kv_cache_hit, probe_type:tool_invoke) - Mapping to Redwood Console event fields and suggested dashboards (latency P50/P95 by probe_type, cache hit ratio over request window) Security and privacy: - Probes intentionally avoid logging PII by default; README highlights fields that could contain user-provided strings and recommends scrubbing. - Relayer includes a configurable filter to drop high-cardinality tags. Documentation additions: - Step-by-step quickstart README with images and expanded troubleshooting - Architecture SVG and example dashboards screenshots - Troubleshooting: common causes for missing probes (sampling env, file permissions) Follow-ups (recommended): - Add TypeScript/Go versions of the same quickstart for SDK parity (tracked ENG-3042) - Add a small demo in the docs site that streams probe events to a live dashboard (opt-in) Related work: ENG-2983 (observability primitives for runtime), PM-1140 (RAG dev experience), SUP-8721 (customer request for debug tooling). Merge notes: - Squash-merged to main after green CI and approvals. - Changelog: docs(quickstarts): add rag embedded debug probes quickstart (release notes above).
